note: Pussytoes (0.9.122): the plantain-leaved pussytoes the catalog had, and four more for a Pussytoes card -- field, small-leaf and rosy pussytoes from North America and mountain everlasting (cat's foot) from Europe, with its 'Rubra'. Natives read against Prairie Moon, New Moon, Minnesota Wildflowers, the Wildflower Center and the USDA Forest Service; mountain everlasting and rosy pussytoes against the RHS, Beth Chatto and Quacking Grass Nursery. Garden.org refused a fetch (403) and Plant Delights rate-limited (429), so 'Nyewood's Variety' and Plant Delights' zones for small-leaf pussytoes were not read and are not used. Sizes and zones conflict between sources; estimates says how each was chosen.

estimates.heightIn: Minnesota Wildflowers 4-9 in, New Moon 6-12 in. Kept at 9 in, in flower; the stems lengthen in seed.
estimates.spread: New Moon 8-18 in, spacing 12-18 in. Kept at 12 in, the record's existing figure.
estimates.bloomMonths: April to June in both; kept at April and May, the record's existing calendar.
estimates.drawing: Basal leaves 1.25-3 in, broadly spoon-shaped, 3-5 veined, grey-green above and silvery beneath; 4-17+ heads in a flat to rounded cluster, phyllary tips white, 'white with a gentle kiss of pink' (New Moon). Evergreen mats (New Moon).

estimates.heightIn: Prairie Moon lists 4 in (the leaves) and flowers 'up to about a foot'; Minnesota Wildflowers 4-16 in. 8 in, in flower.
estimates.spread: Neither gives a spread; Prairie Moon spaces it 2-6 in and both say it runs by stolons into colonies. 12 in, the genus's figure here.
estimates.zones: Prairie Moon gives 3-7 in its text and 3-8 in its table. 3-8.
estimates.bloomMonths: April, May and June in both.
estimates.drawing: Leaves 0.5-2.5 in, narrowly spatulate, one vein, grey-green above and silvery beneath; mid and upper stem leaves end in a papery white flag; 2-8 heads in a flat to rounded cluster, white to pale pink. Semi-evergreen.
estimates.roles: Host plant for the American lady (both pages). Prairie Moon says deer and rabbits avoid it.

estimates.heightIn: Minnesota Wildflowers: flowering stalks commonly under 4 in, rarely 6; the Wildflower Center up to about 6 in. 4 in.
estimates.spread: Neither gives a spread. 12 in, the genus's figure here.
estimates.zones: Neither page gives zones. Wikipedia says hardy to zone 4; a retailer found in search gives 3-8, and it is native in Minnesota and the Canadian prairies. 3-8.
estimates.bloomMonths: Minnesota Wildflowers May-June; the Wildflower Center July-September, a high-country season. May and June.
estimates.drawing: Leaves 1/3-1 1/3 in, narrowly spatulate, silvery from dense hairs on both faces; 2-7 heads, female heads 3/8-1/2 in, phyllary tips white, pink, red or brown.

estimates.heightIn: RHS up to 10 cm; a nursery found in search gives flowers at 8 in; floras 8-40 cm. 6 in.
estimates.zones: RHS H5; a plant guide found in search gives 3a-9b. It ranges into Alaska and the high Rockies, so cold is not its limit. 3-8.
estimates.bloomMonths: The Forest Service says spring; RHS lists late spring to early summer. May and June.
estimates.drawing: Narrowly obovate leaves, grey-green above, white beneath, an evergreen mat (RHS, Forest Service); up to 20 heads in a cluster (Minnesota Wildflowers), small yellow florets inside rose-pink bracts (Forest Service). RHS Award of Garden Merit.

estimates.heightIn: RHS up to 10 cm; Wikipedia 10-20 cm. 6 in.
estimates.spread: RHS 0.1-0.5 m; Beth Chatto 30 cm for 'Rubra'. 12 in.
estimates.zones: The RHS gives H5, its own scale. US nurseries for 'Rubra': Quacking Grass 5-9, Ferris Seeds 4-7 (in search). It is native from Britain to Siberia, so cold is not its limit; summer heat and wet are. 4-8.
estimates.bloomMonths: RHS late spring and early summer; Beth Chatto May and June.
estimates.nativeTo: Wikipedia: a Eurasian species, in North America only on the Aleutian Islands, which a continental range cannot express. Europe and Asia.
estimates.drawing: A semi-evergreen mat of spoon-shaped leaves, white-hairy beneath (RHS), 4 by 1 cm (Wikipedia); heads 6-12 mm, the male plants' whiter than the female's pale pink.

estimates.heightIn: RHS around 15 cm in its text, Beth Chatto 10 cm, Quacking Grass 3-4 in. Inherits the species' 6 in.
estimates.bloom: Reddish-pink (RHS), red-pink (Quacking Grass), rose-pink (Beth Chatto), over silver-grey rosettes.
